description:
RFC 8620 §5.6 maxChanges pagination requires that newState in a truncated /changes response point to the last returned item's state, not the current store state. Without per-row counters, truncation produces a newState that skips intermediate changes on the next poll.

The store uses per-row changed_at_counter on messages, contacts, and chats (added in migrations V8/V9/V10) with a separate get_changes_since_ordered() method that returns counters alongside IDs. This lets JMAP handlers compute the correct newState for a truncated page without a second query.

The dual method design (get_changes_since for simple cases, get_changes_since_ordered for paginated cases) with clear docs warning against mixing them is the right call — a single method that always returns counters would have been equally valid but adds caller complexity for the common case.

This is worth defending if someone suggests simplifying to a single state-counter approach (e.g., just return current state for all truncated responses). RFC 8620 §5.6 compliance requires the per-item counter approach.
title: DECISION: per-row changed_at_counter for JMAP changes pagination
